findings.summary: The actively-used @anthropic-ai/sdk dependency is declared with a caret on a 0.x version, so npm can never resolve past the 0.104.x patch line.
findings.evidence: dependencies: "@anthropic-ai/sdk": "^0.104.1". Caret on a 0.x package expands to >=0.104.1 <0.105.0, not <1.0.0. The package is actively imported (files/src/main/claudeAssistant.ts) and the SDK is still pre-1.0 with releases well past 0.104 (0.110.x line), all of which this range excludes.
findings.recommendation: Widen the range to "~0.110" (or the current 0.x line) and re-run `npm install` to refresh the lockfile; add @anthropic-ai/sdk to a Renovate/Dependabot config so 0.x minor bumps are proposed automatically rather than requiring a manual range edit each time.

findings.summary: The project has no automated vulnerability scan and no dependency-update bot, so nothing surfaces advisories or proposes upgrades for its 25 declared dependencies.
findings.evidence: No .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, .circleci/config.yml, renovate.json, .dependabot/config.yml, or .github/dependabot.yml exists anywhere in the repo (the only tracked YAML is docker-compose.yml). Combined with the caret ranges used on every dependency (e.g. "electron": "^42.4.1", "better-sqlite3": "^12.11.1", "serialport": "^12.0.0"), there is no CI gate running `npm ci` + `npm audit` to detect when a resolved transitive version becomes vulnerable.
findings.recommendation: Add .github/workflows/deps.yml running `npm ci && npm audit --audit-level=high` on push and on a weekly schedule, and commit .github/dependabot.yml with a weekly npm ecosystem update for files/.

findings.summary: electron-store is declared as a runtime dependency but is never imported anywhere in the source tree.
findings.evidence: dependencies: "electron-store": "^8.0.0". A grep for `electron-store`, `electron_store`, and `new Store` across every .ts/.tsx/.js file under files/ returns zero matches; persistence is implemented in files/src/main/storageService.ts using node fs plus a lazy `require('better-sqlite3')`. The pinned major is also several releases behind the current line, so it is dead weight that still ships in the packaged app.
findings.recommendation: Remove "electron-store" from dependencies in files/package.json and re-run `npm install` to drop it and its transitives from files/package-lock.json.

findings.summary: package.json declares no engines field, so no Node or npm version constraint is enforced at install time.
findings.evidence: No "engines" key is present in files/package.json. The project is a native-module Electron app (better-sqlite3, serialport both require node-gyp ABI matching) and @types/node is pinned at "^22.0.0", but nothing prevents an install under a mismatched Node major.
findings.recommendation: Add "engines": {"node": ">=22 <23", "npm": ">=10"} to files/package.json and set engine-strict=true in an .npmrc so a mismatched runtime fails the install rather than producing a broken native build.

findings.summary: package.json has no overrides block, leaving no mechanism to force-pin a vulnerable transitive dependency ahead of an upstream fix.
findings.evidence: No "overrides" (npm) or "resolutions" (yarn) key is present in files/package.json, despite a committed npm lockfile (files/package-lock.json, lockfileVersion 3) and deep transitive trees under electron-builder, webpack, and exceljs.
findings.recommendation: Add an empty "overrides": {} block to files/package.json as the documented escape hatch, so an emergency transitive pin is a one-line edit rather than a lockfile hand-edit.

findings.summary: recharts is declared as a runtime dependency but no chart component from it is imported anywhere in the source tree.
findings.evidence: dependencies: "recharts": "^2.0.0". A grep for `recharts`, `LineChart`, `ResponsiveContainer`, and `AreaChart` across every .ts/.tsx file under files/ returns zero matches, including in the graphing-oriented screens (LiveScreen.tsx, CompareScreen.tsx).
findings.recommendation: Remove "recharts" from dependencies in files/package.json and re-run `npm install` to drop it from files/package-lock.json; re-add it explicitly if charting is implemented later.
